name: Question 11
problem:
The second-order differential equation $3{y}^{″}+9\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,{y}^{′}+y=0$
can be expressed as the matrix equation ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t),$ where 

$$
x(t)=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,A=[\begin{aligned}a & b \\ c & d\end{aligned}],\,y(t)={x}_{1}(t),\,{y}^{′}(t)={x}_{2}(t).
$$

Find the matrix $A.$

The second-order differential equation 3y″+9sin⁡ty′+y=0 can be expressed as the matrix equation x′(t)=Ax(t), where

x(t)=[x1x2],A=[abcd],y(t)=x1(t),y′(t)=x2(t). Find the matrix A.

a
[−sin⁡t3−301]
b
[01−13−3sin⁡t]
c
[10−sin⁡t3−3]
d
[01−3sin⁡t−13]
e
[0sin⁡t−130]
